$comment: #890 W0 — the pinned device matrix for every scheduled mobile lane. An unpinned device makes a screen-size or OS-behaviour regression indistinguishable from a runner-image roll. Each entry names the device, the OS, and — where the pin diverges from what a member actually holds — why that divergence is deliberate and recorded rather than accidental.

ios.why: A current Pro is the reference phone: it carries the Dynamic Island inset the shell's safe-area math is written against, and macos-26 images ship it. fallbackDeviceNames is an ORDERED ladder, not a wildcard — a runner image that drops the pin still resolves to a named device the roster has seen, and the resolver prints which rung it landed on so the substitution is visible in the log rather than silent.

divergences.why: Only x86_64 is accelerated by /dev/kvm on the Linux runner; an arm64 image runs under full emulation and every journey times out. The divergence is real — JSC/Hermes codegen, NEON paths in the tunnel native module, and op-sqlite's compiled extensions all differ by ABI — so it is recorded here rather than assumed away. The arm64 evidence a member's phone actually produces is a release-cadence device-farm spend, deferred in #890's non-goals.

The AVD snapshot cache key (avd-api34-…) is what makes this lane affordable; bumping the API level invalidates it and costs a cold boot on every run until it re-banks. Bump deliberately with the cache key's trailing -vN, never as a drive-by.
